chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abdul Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who proposed to a man for a daughter of his from a free woman. So when it was the night she was to enter upon her husband, he made another daughter of his from a slave girl go over to him instead. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She would be returned to her father, and his wife would be returned to him, and her dower would be upon her father.'

key_terms.مَهِيرَةٍ: Free woman (as opposed to a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a father substitutes a slave girl for his free daughter on the wedding night?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the legal remedy for 'ghurur' (deception) in marriage, specifically when a father substitutes a slave girl for his free daughter on the wedding night. It establishes that the substituted slave returns to her father, the original daughter returns to the groom, and the dowry remains the responsibility of the deceiving father. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on consent and the specific status of the bride in determining the validity of the marriage contract.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Abdul Hameed, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who proposed to a man for a daughter of his from a free ones. So when it was the night when she was supposed to enter upon her husband, he made another daughter of his from the slave girl to go over to him instead’. He<sup>asws</sup> said :’She would be returned to her father, and his wife would be returned to him, and her dower would be upon her father’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from ‘Abd al-Hamid from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who proposes marriage to a man for his daughter for a certain amount of mahr (dower) but in the night of their going to bed he sends his other daughter who is from a slave-girl. He (the Imam) said, ‘He returns her to her father who must send his wife to him and her mahr (dower) is on her father.’”
